text: Last time, I said the family works the other way round.
Today, we learn the family trick for taking away.
One lower bead on the ones rod, and one lower bead on the tens rod.
The big friend says: add four to the ones rod, then take ten off the tens rod.
Is there room for four more lower beads on the ones rod?
The upper bead is up, and the lower beads are almost full.
To add four: take away one, then add five.
The big friend and the small friend, side by side.
That team is called the family.
Look: room on the ones rod?
Call: no room, call the family.
The big friend says: minus six equals plus four, minus ten.
The small friend swaps plus four for minus one, plus five.
So the family says: minus six equals minus one, plus five, minus ten.
Minus ten takes four too many.
So we add four back first.
Plus six was plus one, minus five, plus ten.
So which finger now, thumb or index?
Lower beads first, then the upper bead.
Eleven take away six is five.
Two lower beads on the ones rod, and two lower beads on the tens rod.
Room for three more lower beads?
Minus seven equals minus two, plus five, minus ten.
Twenty-two take away seven is fifteen!
And subscribe, the next trick is a big one.
On the ones rod, three lower beads.
Then on the tens rod, four lower beads and the upper bead.
Thumb for the lower beads, index finger for the upper bead.
How many more lower beads fit?
Minus eight equals minus three, plus five, minus ten.
Ninety-three take away eight is eighty-five!
Plus family: plus lower beads, minus five, plus ten.
Minus family: minus lower beads, plus five, minus ten.
Minus six, minus seven, minus eight, minus nine.
On the ones rod, four lower beads.
Then on the tens rod, three lower beads and the upper bead.
Nine is five and four more.
So how many lower beads come off first?
Minus nine equals minus four, plus five, minus ten.
All down, so all index finger.
Eighty-four take away nine is seventy-five!
You did Look, Call, Move all by yourself.
